title: Federal Reserve Publishes FEDS Note on Manufacturing Heterogeneity
discussion_signal: The post relays a Federal Reserve FEDS Note using Census BTOS data and says aggregate manufacturing indicators can move together while industry-level data reveals substantial subsector heterogeneity. It highlights a tariff-exposure case in which more exposed subsectors show faster price growth. This is an adjacent comparator for the atlas misallocation record: both warn that aggregate manufacturing measures can conceal where adjustment and pressure are concentrated, but the FEDS Note does not estimate the atlas record's margin-versus-input-mix decomposition.
linked_research_question: When aggregate manufacturing looks stable, do margin distortions, input-mix differences, or policy exposure identify the plants and subsectors carrying the adjustment?
limits: The post relays a different Federal Reserve paper and is an adjacent comparator, not the same study as the atlas anchor
Subsector price growth does not establish allocative inefficiency, plant-level productivity, or worker outcomes
The discussion does not independently verify the underlying estimates
